The *Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 104) is a canonical Pali verse text located in the *Therāpadāna* within the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. As part of the biographical poetry collection dedicated to Buddhist elder monks (theras), the text recounts the spiritual merits and past karmic actions of the thera Ñāṇasaññika [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral catalogs five modern translations of the poem across five languages [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are identified by DharmaNexus with a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus records 65 matching text-reuse passages shared across 16 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial reuse partner is the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), sharing 25 matches comprising 2,564 characters, with a primary alignment covering segments §1.1–6.3 of the apadāna with commentary segments §1359–1370 [DharmaNexus]. Additional segments are cited in the second part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (§4.3–6.3 ↔ §1975–1978) [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Therāpadāna* collection itself, formulaic verses—predominantly spanning segments §4.1–8.1—are shared with several other apadāna texts, most notably another poem bearing the identical name *Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 130), as well as the *Saṁghupaṭṭhākattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 182), *Bandhujīvakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 184), and *Madhupiṇḍikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 99) [DharmaNexus].
